text: (4 marks) a. Calculate the number of moles of carbon monoxide molecules in 1.20 x 1025 molecules of carbon monoxide. Show your working clearly. (2 marks) b. Calculate the number of hydrogen atoms in 6.25 moles of H2SO4. (2 marks)
html:
(4 marks)

a. Calculate the number of moles of carbon monoxide molecules in 1.20 x 1025 molecules of carbon monoxide. Show your working clearly. (2 marks)

b. Calculate the number of hydrogen atoms in 6.25 moles of H2SO4. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
8. (4 marks)

a. Calculate the number of moles of carbon monoxide molecules in 1.20 x 1025 moles of carbon monoxide. Show your working clearly. (2 marks)

n(CO)=N6.022×1023=1.20×10256.022×1023=19.9mol

b. Calculate the number of hydrogen atoms in 6.25 moles of H2SO4. (2 marks)

N(H2SO4)=n×6.022×1023=6.25×6.022×1023=3.76×1024

N(H)=N(H2SO4)×2=7.53×1024

Octane (C8H1) is the primary component of petrol. The fuel tank of a car can store an average of 60 L of octane. Energy is released by combustion the octane according to the following equation:

b. A small amount of chlorine gas is bubbled through methylbenzene: (2 marks)

c. A small amount of methylpropane is added to an excess of bromine in the presence of UV light.

(3 marks)
answerHtml:
Teacher review required. The guide’s methylbenzene side-chain chlorination requires UV light, which is not specified in the paper. Review reaction conditions.

Supplied reaction products, with structures transcribed as editable condensed formulae:

(a) CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂CH₃ + H₂O → HOCH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (H₂SO₄ catalyst). The question allows one product isomer.

(b) C₆H₅CH₃ + Cl₂ → C₆H₅CH₂Cl + HCl (requires UV).

(c) (CH₃)₃CH + 10Br₂ → (CBr₃)₃CBr + 10HBr (UV, excess bromine).
